newsitem.title: UK: Strike threat lifted at Ford UK plant.
newsitem.headline: Strike threat lifted at Ford UK plant.

text.p: The threat of national strikes at U.S. carmaker Ford Co's British plants was lifted on Friday as a transport union spokeswoman said agreement had been reached in talks over the future of Ford's plant at Halewood, Merseyside, northwest England.
She said further details would be available at a news conference to be held later on Friday.
The spokeswoman for the Transport and General Workers Union (T&G) said the agreement to secure the long-term future of Halewood was regarded by the union as an "achievement".

The agreement comes after two-day talks between Ford's European head Jac Nasser and union leaders from the T&G and the Amalgamated Engineers and Electricians Unions (AEEU) in a last ditch effort by the workers to try and save 1,300 jobs set to go after Ford's decision last month to move production of its new Escort model to continental Europe.

Unions told reporters that under the deal there would be fewer than the 1,300 job losses originally planned at Halewood. Production of the Escort would still switch to Germany and Spain but union leaders said mainstream models would continue to be made at Halewood.
A strike ballot of all Ford workers in Britain has been called off and the deal is expected to be put to a meeting of Halewood workers next week.
